2608.03722.title: When Outputs Disperse, Does Epistemic Revision Follow? A Black-Box Coupling Diagnostic for Machine Collectives
2608.03722.paper_summary: Collective intelligence research treats disagreement as evidence of epistemic diversity: if agents express different views, the group should retain capacity to revise. In LLM collectives this proxy can break: agents can produce diverse-looking arguments while preserving the same conclusion. We operationalize dispersion-revision coupling: the degree to which an intervention that verifiably increases the dispersion of a collective's outputs in embedding space is accompanied by genuine revision of its epistemic stance rather than premise-preserving reformulation. The diagnostic is black-box: it operates on generated text alone and makes no claims about the internal representations of the generating models. Two channels are measured independently: an output channel, the Coherence Index (CI), verifies that the intervention changed output dispersion; an epistemic channel, per-turn stance annotation, measures whether the collective revised. We propose CI with the Meta-Predictive Clarity System (MPCS), which inserts a Re-Differentiation Protocol (RDP) when outputs over-converge, as a reusable method for estimating this coupling regime. We evaluate five-agent collectives from two configurations (gpt-4o-mini and gemini-2.5-flash; 310 paired episodes per condition). On gpt-4o-mini, conditional dissent improves false-premise recovery by +17.7 points (p<1e-6) while static persona diversity harms recovery (-8.1, p=.007). On gemini-2.5-flash, the same intervention at a comparable budget yields no gain (26.1% vs 27.1%, p=.84) despite a verified dispersion drop; the two treatment effects differ from each other (z=3.79, p<.001). Mechanism tagging shows Gemini preserves the false premise via intra-framework dissent: 94% of tagged post-RDP responses reformulate rather than concede (vs 24% on GPT). We recommend reporting per-intervention stance shift and premise-preservation rate alongside accuracy.
2608.03722.paper_summary_zh: 集體智慧研究將分歧視為認識論多樣性的證據：如果代理人表達不同的觀點，該群體應保留修正的能力。 在大型語言模型（LLM）集體中，這一代理可能會破裂：代理人可以產生看似多樣的論點，同時保持相同的結論。 我們操作化了分散-修正耦合：可驗證地增加集體輸出在嵌入空間中的分散程度的干預，是否伴隨著其認識論立場的真正修正，而不是保持前提的重新表述。 診斷是黑箱的：它僅在生成的文本上運作，並不對生成模型的內部表示提出任何主張。 兩個通道獨立測量：一個輸出通道，即一致性指數（CI），驗證干預是否改變了輸出分散；一個認識論通道，即每回合的立場註釋，測量集體是否進行了修正。 我們提出了與元預測清晰系統（MPCS）結合的CI，當輸出過度收斂時插入重新區分協議（RDP），作為估計這一耦合制度的可重用方法。 我們評估了來自兩個配置（gpt-4o-mini和gemini-2.5-flash）的五代理集體（每個條件310對應的實例）。 在gpt-4o-mini上，有條件的異議使得錯誤前提的恢復提高了17.7分（p<1e-6），而靜態角色多樣性則損害了恢復（-8.1，p=.007）。 在gemini-2.5-flash上，相同的干預在可比較的預算下沒有產生增益（26.1%對27.1%，p=.84），儘管經過驗證的分散下降；兩種處理效果彼此不同（z=3.79，p<.001）。 機制標記顯示，Gemini通過框架內的異議保留了錯誤前提：94%的標記後RDP響應進行了重新表述，而不是讓步（相比之下，GPT為24%）。 我們建議報告每次干預的立場變化和前提保留率，並與準確性一起報告。
